name: Attribuly
summary: Recovers abandoned carts Klaviyo misses: identifies visitors, syncs intent signals back into Klaviyo and lets an AI agent send a personalised recovery email.
best_for: stores already running Klaviyo or Omnisend at volume, with enough traffic for identity resolution to work and enough recovered revenue to cover a plan priced on their GMV
skip_if: you do not run Klaviyo or another supported email platform, since the product feeds them rather than replacing them; or you want a price that stays put as you grow, because both paid plans step up with your GMV
honest_knock: The pricing has moved twice in three months. In August and September 2026 the listing went from free straight to $450 or $500 a month; in October recovery became ReCapture at the larger of $100 or 10% of what it recovered; on 17 November 2026 the listing showed Free, Pro at $99 and Enterprise at $219, both priced on your store's GMV, with cart recovery inside Enterprise and anonymous visitor identification (Capture) as an add on from $450 a month. The GMV scale is steep: Enterprise is $219 below $250K of annual GMV and $549 from $1M, so read the tier against your own sales before the trial ends. It is still an add on rather than a replacement: the pitch is explicitly that it recovers carts “Klaviyo misses” and syncs identity signals back into Klaviyo, so you pay for this on top of an email platform you already pay for.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · per month below $250K of GMV over the last 12 months
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/attribuly, attribuly.com/pricing and attribuly.com/pricing-retention/, and in our own test session on 17 November 2026; the plan ladder changed again after 14 October 2026) Three plans on the listing: Free, Pro at $99 a month and Enterprise at $219 a month, the paid two with a 7 day free trial and both marked “We charge based on your GMV”. attribuly.com/pricing sets those two prices by the store's GMV over the last 12 months, Pro and Enterprise respectively: $99 and $219 below $250K, $139 and $329 from $250K to $500K, $209 and $429 from $500K to $1M, $299 and $549 from $1M to $2.5M, $489 and $799 from $2.5M to $5M, $629 and $1,129 from $5M to $7.5M, $849 and $1,529 from $7.5M to $10M, $1,029 and $1,849 from $10M to $15M, $1,399 and $2,529 from $15M to $20M, $1,699 and $3,079 from $20M to $30M and $2,299 and $4,229 from $30M to $40M; above $40M it is contact sales. Free costs $0 and recovers the first $1,000 of email revenue; it includes multi touch attribution, new customer CPA benchmarks by cohort and a Klaviyo or ESP missed revenue audit. Pro adds cross channel attribution, server side tracking, data sync to ad platforms, GA4 enrichment, a post purchase survey and unlimited tracking links. Enterprise adds the recovery of abandoned carts Klaviyo misses (ReCapture), checkout tracking on Shopify Plus, AI attribution across views and clicks, product analytics, a raw data API and a dedicated success manager. Capture, which identifies anonymous visitors and enriches US emails, is priced separately: $450 a month for 1,500 emails ($0.30 an email), $800 for 3,000 ($0.27) and $2,100 for 10,000 ($0.21), with 25,000 and more quoted; unused emails roll over. The separate ReCapture page, attribuly.com/pricing-retention/, still sells recovery on its own as pay for performance: the larger of $100 a month or 10% of the incremental revenue it recovers, with a quote from $12,000,000 of annual GMV; neither page says how that offer relates to Enterprise, which includes ReCapture. The plans we read on 14 October 2026, ReCapture at the larger of $100 or a 10% revenue share and Capture at $450 a month flat, are no longer on the listing. All charges are billed in USD, recurring and usage based charges every 30 days. On 17 November 2026 the listing showed 4.8 from 172 reviews. In our own test session the app opened on a choice of email platform (Klaviyo, MambaSMS, Omnisend or CartSee) and its onboarding would not continue without connecting Klaviyo, so we reached no plan or payment screen.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested the start of Attribuly on a Shopify development store: the install, a welcome survey and then four screen steps to a wall. The first screen offered only Klaviyo, MambaSMS, Omnisend and CartSee, with Book a Demo for stores on another e-mail platform; the onboarding asked to connect a Klaviyo account and its Continue button stayed greyed out; the link for an attribution-only set-up did nothing when clicked twice. So the first result was not reached, no plan or checkout screen was seen, and the prices come from the listing and not from a test. The uninstall dialog was seen and the app was uninstalled afterwards. Install: the install form of the App Store listing (English) was submitted in our own tab at about 19:00; the Shopify dialog Install app asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked at about 19:01. The app went through a page of the vendor (Verifying your session authorization) and was open at about 19:02. Welcome to Attribuly asked how we first heard about it (Shopify App Store was chosen) and had a required field about what we searched for; a popup about a new attribution template was closed. No password, card or phone number was asked. The admin was in English. Core action, set up abandoned-cart recovery or attribution: NOT reached. At about 19:04 the screen Choose your ESP offered Klaviyo (Selected), MambaSMS, Omnisend and CartSee, with the line Not using above ESPs or want to identify anonymous visitors? Book a Demo and the line Only want to use Attribution? Click here to set up. The link Click here to set up was clicked twice and did nothing visible (no new page and no new tab). Start email recovery led to the onboarding Find the shoppers Klaviyo can't see, with four steps (Connect Klaviyo, Select events, Enable App embed, Activate Klaviyo flow) and the text Connect your Klaviyo account to start recovering missed revenue; the button Continue stayed greyed out as long as no Klaviyo account was connected. Connecting Klaviyo was not done, because it needs an account at another vendor. So there were 4 screen steps up to the wall, about 5 minutes after the start, and no first result: no recovery e-mail, no attribution view and no measurement. What the app looked like in Shopify after the install (Manage app): Pixels Disconnected, Extensions 0 active, Expiring access tokens Missing, Enforced IP restrictions Enforced; access to Online Store, Customers and Discounts (view and edit), Orders and Products (view only) and Marketing and Store analytics (view and edit). Plans: no plan choice and no subscription screen was seen in the app, because the onboarding blocked first. The charges address of the app in Shopify (charges, pricing plans) gave There's no page at this address. The Shopify screen Approve subscription was not reached, so nothing was approved. From the App Store listing of 17 November (not a test result): Free plan available and Free trial available; Free recovers $1000 of e-mail revenue and has multi-touch attribution, new customer CPA benchmarks by cohort and a missed revenue audit for Klaviyo or another ESP; Pro $99 a month and Enterprise $219 a month, both charged based on the GMV (with Capture, to identify anonymous visitors, as an add-on on Enterprise), with a 7-day free trial on both; all charges in USD, recurring and usage-based charges billed every 30 days. Difference with the dossier (from the listing, not from the app): the dossier of 14 October gives ReCapture at $100 a month plus a 10% revenue share and Capture at $450 a month flat; the listing now shows Pro $99 and Enterprise $219, GMV based, so the dossier prices are out of date or renamed; the rating on the listing is 4.8 from 172 reviews (the dossier says 167). The price fields are not changed here; this is for the price bundle. Checkout: NOT reached, no plan screen and no Shopify approval screen were seen, no card was entered and nothing was paid. Cancelling: no paid plan ran, so nothing could be cancelled; the uninstall dialog was seen: it says that after uninstalling any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information, and it has a list of reasons (Testing multiple apps, Too expensive and others). Not tested: connecting Klaviyo or Omnisend, abandoned-cart recovery, e-mail, anonymous visitors (Capture), the attribution dashboard, the app embed, the ROI guarantee, paid plans, payment, a plan choice in the app and Book a Demo. Clean up: Attribuly was uninstalled at about 19:12 with the reason Testing multiple apps and no longer appeared in the list of installed apps; other apps were not touched; our own tab was closed. The clock times in the notes can be a few minutes off. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The set-up needed a connected account at another vendor (Klaviyo) before Continue worked; the link for an attribution-only set-up did nothing; stores on other e-mail platforms were pointed to Book a Demo; no plan or price was shown in the app; and the charges address of the app in Shopify gave an empty page.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?

Can you publish the price or the rule?
Our price check could not put a number on this part of the cost: Capture is an add on at $450 a month for 1,500 emails, $800 for 3,000 and $2,100 for 10,000. Can you publish the price or the rule?

Our price check could not put a number on this part of the cost: The separate ReCapture offer is billed as the larger of $100 or 10% of the incremental revenue it recovers each month; that depends on recovered revenue, which this engine does not take as input. Can you publish the price or the rule?
